literal: Nest having become alone to be left behind, bird having flown like that indeed, body-with life-between friendship.
translation: The bond between the body and the soul is just like that of a bird that flies away, leaving its empty nest behind.
modern: உடம்பிற்கும் உயிருக்கும் இடையிலான உறவு, பறவை தன் கூட்டினைத் தனியே விட்டுவிட்டுப் பறந்து செல்வதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the transient nature of life using a vivid metaphor. The word 'kuṭampai' can mean either a nest or an egg-shell; in either sense, it represents the physical body left behind. Just as a bird eventually flies away, leaving its former home empty and alone, the soul (uyir) departs from the body (uṭampu) when its time comes. The 'friendship' or bond (naṭpu) between body and soul is temporary, emphasizing that physical existence is not permanent.
